history.note: harness until the mode-cutoff restart (borg-zoo#54). The runner and observer are unchanged at the new pin; the bump keeps the harness commit at the specimens' tree after the 0100/0101/0101a fixes. A proposed runner change that would have recorded the applied configuration text (better-borg-c PR 435) was closed as mis-filed and is not needed: configuration_sha256 already identifies what a run applied.
live watchdog read could abort a run on a split UTF-8 character (better-borg-c#220); fixed by 56ccf741. The observer is unchanged between the two pins.

harness.note: The better-borg-c runner and observer at this commit build and run every specimen. A specimen is the game and Borg source at its own ref; the observer instrumentation comes from the harness commit. It applies to specimens of kind "better-borg-c" (the default). Specimens of kind "borg-rs" are built and run by borg-rs's own harness at the specimen's ref (harness/build.sh and the borgh frontend). This pin is also a specimen ref (4.2.6-bbc-9ca98661): the harness bumped with the mode-cutoff restart so runner and specimens move together (borg-zoo#54).

default.description: Compatibility alias for experiments recorded before the mode cutoff (2026-11-10, borg-zoo#54): settings {}, so every mode stays on the build's own default - and borg_munchkin_by_class defaults TRUE only from better-borg-c fd683ced (PR 302). The same profile name is a different game on either side of that commit, so default is NOT comparable across it: an experiment that touches a post-cutoff better-borg-c specimen must name a mode profile (normal, munchkin-class, munchkin-on, lunal) instead; plan rejects default there. Experiments recorded before the cutoff keep default under their "pre_cutoff" note.

4.2.6-rs-m10.label: borg-rs M10 (tag 4.2.6-impact-v10): the Rust Borg carrying better-borg-c milestone 10's units (borg-rs#23, PR 24; qualified pass, findings addressed, owner accepted). No new tracker carry: I-001 and I-002 are owner-directed local improvements carried for C/Rust parity, and the 0099 crash guard borg-rs has had since milestone 9 needed a comment sync only. 131/131 C/Rust parity; the pre-existing munchkin stair livelock case (better-borg-c#204) now completes in both roles. The engine is unchanged since 4.2.6-impact-v4, so its game still differs from better-borg-c M10 by that tag's engine correction (neo-angband-tracker#474). Like M8 and M9, its default already includes the munchkin-by-class start, inherited unchanged from M8.

4.2.6-rs-m10-c.label: borg-rs 4.2.6-impact-v10, C Borg: the C Borg in borg-rs's tree with better-borg-c milestone 10's units (I-001 lone-adjacent-kill retreat guard, I-002 flee healing, and the 0099 crash-guard comment sync - no new tracker carry), under the borgh frontend. The engine is unchanged since 4.2.6-impact-v4, so it keeps that tag's engine correction (neo-angband-tracker#474).

4.2.6-rs-m9.label: borg-rs M9 (tag 4.2.6-impact-v9): the Rust Borg carrying better-borg-c milestone 9's fixes (borg-rs#21, PR 22; qualified pass, all findings addressed, re-review pass, owner accepted; two upstream crash patches carried with a narrow local guard, reported on better-borg-c#375 and #377). The engine is unchanged since 4.2.6-impact-v4, so its game still differs from better-borg-c M9 by that tag's engine correction (neo-angband-tracker#474). Like M8, its default already includes the munchkin-by-class start, inherited unchanged from M8, so the munchkin-wdr profile is expected to be a no-op here too, though not independently re-confirmed.
